gloss: to feel rough; to be coarse to the touch

definitions.gloss: to feel rough; to be coarse; to have a gritty texture
definitions.explanation: Describes a surface or texture that feels rough, gritty, or unsmooth when touched. Derives from the onomatopoeia ざらざら.

examples.japanese: {乾燥|かんそう}すると{手|て}がざらついてくる。
examples.english: When it gets dry, my hands start to feel rough.

examples.japanese: このタオルは{洗|あら}いすぎてざらついた{手触|てざわ}りになってしまった。
examples.english: This towel has been washed so many times that it has a rough feel to it.

notes:
A verb derived from the onomatopoeia ざらざら (rough, gritty texture). Very commonly used when talking about skin care, fabric quality, and surface textures.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {肌|はだ}がざらつく: skin feels rough
- {手触|てざわ}りがざらつく: the texture feels rough
- {表面|ひょうめん}がざらつく: the surface is rough
- ざらついた{感触|かんしょく}: a rough feeling/sensation

RELATED WORDS:
- ざらざら: rough; gritty (onomatopoeia) — the base mimetic word
- すべすべ: smooth; silky — the opposite texture
- かさつく: to be dry and rough (skin) — focuses on dryness rather than texture
- ごわつく: to feel stiff and rough (fabric) — implies thicker, stiffer roughness

COMMON PATTERNS:
Godan verb conjugating with く. The て-form is ざらついて. Often used in the ている form to describe an ongoing state: ざらついている (is rough).

forms.label: Past polite

forms.negative: ざらついていなかった
